messages.subject: Spatial clustering across multiple samples
parts:
Hi,
I have a question: I combined the data from different samples (same tissue type) and would like to cluster all my samples into a few tissue subtypes (which should be present in all samples). When running the spatial shrunken centroids, I get a very large number of clusters out and most of them are specific to one or two of the samples, overall it looks very messy. So i was wondering whether the way the algorithm is implemented makes it even suitable for merged samples and take into account sample name on top of the pixel coordinates?
Thanks a lot,
Ilona

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Spatial clustering across multiple samples
parts:
The method itself is suitable and does not care what samples/runs a pixel came from; it only looks at the mass spectra/peaks and those of neighboring pixels.

However, it's very common that the run-to-run and/or sample-to-sample variation may be larger than the variation between tissue subtypes, and this can have a major impact on the data analysis

Ideally, normalization would fix this -- and careful pre-processing can help -- but even very good normalization with internal standards can only really do something about the run-to-run variation, and not so much sample-to-sample variation.
